lines.japanese: 十五分足らずのショート・ホームルームは、長いようでも短いようでもあった。
lines.english: The short homeroom lasted less than fifteen minutes. Somehow it felt both long and short.

lines.japanese: 早く終わってほしいという願いと、いざ並んで歩きだしたら上手く話せるだろうかという不安が、僕の胸の浅いところで激しくせめぎ合っていたせいだと思う。
lines.english: I suppose that was because two forces were warring fiercely in the shallows of my chest: the wish for it to end at once, and the fear that once we fell into step together, I would not know what to say.

lines.japanese: どきどきわくわく──なんていう、ありふれた擬態語が思いうかんだ。懐かしい感覚。僕はどきどきならよく知ってるけど、わくわくにはあまり馴染みがなかった。
lines.english: My heart pounding, my spirits soaring—the most ordinary phrases came to mind. It was an almost forgotten sensation. I knew all about pounding hearts. Soaring spirits were far less familiar.

lines.japanese: 「──なので、えー、充分に気を付けてください」
lines.english: “—and so, ah, please take every precaution.”

lines.japanese: もどかしい退屈から逃れるべく、僕は担任の事務的な声に耳を傾けた。
lines.english: To escape the torment of waiting, I turned my attention to our homeroom teacher’s bureaucratic voice.

lines.japanese: 「次が、えー、卒業文集の制作について」
lines.english: “Next, ah, the preparation of the graduation anthology.”

lines.japanese: 棒読み恩ティーとあだ名される恩田先生は、きょうも職員会議で配られたプリントをほぼそのまま読みあげている。
lines.english: Ms. Onda, nicknamed Monotone O-T, was once again reading almost verbatim from a handout distributed at the faculty meeting.

lines.japanese: 「えー卒文制作、こちらは残念なことに、例年生徒たちの参加意欲が薄いという実情です。彼らも……失礼、皆さんも、大変な時期ではありますが──」
lines.english: “Ah, the graduation anthology. Regrettably, the truth is that every year, the students show very little desire to participate. They are… excuse me, all of you are going through a difficult time, but—”

lines.japanese: 「個々人の積極的な自主性を育むよう、生徒たちに指導……失礼、ええとまあ、そんな感じで、要は頑張れってことです」
lines.english: “‘Guide the students in such a way as to nurture each individual’s active independence’… Excuse me. Well, something like that. The point is, do your best.”

lines.japanese: カンペを読んでいることなど隠そうともしない潔さ。僕らと十も違わない、教員としてはまだ新人と呼んで差しつかえないひとだけど、彼女からは若さゆえの情熱みたいなものがまったく感じられない。
lines.english: There was an admirable honesty in her complete refusal to hide the fact that she was reading from a crib sheet. She was less than ten years older than we were, young enough to be called a novice teacher, yet she gave off no trace of youthful passion whatsoever.

lines.japanese: けれどその「走らない」やっつけ感が、逆に生徒からは好印象だったりする。僕らが理想とする教師像は熱血系の兄貴分じゃない。余計なお世話を働かない無味無臭のサラリーマンだ。
lines.english: Yet the perfunctory way she never went the extra mile only endeared her to the students. Our ideal teacher was no hot-blooded big-brother figure. It was a bland, odorless office drone who never burdened us with unwanted concern.

lines.japanese: そうして静かな教室に広がる恩田先生の声は、今日も僕の耳を右から左へ通りすぎていった。
lines.english: And so, in the quiet classroom, Ms. Onda’s voice passed in through one of my ears and out the other as usual.

lines.japanese: というより、今日は格別だ。今日は落ちつかない。椅子に座っていても血がふつふつと騒いでる感じがして、どうにもじっとしていられなかった。
lines.english: Actually, today was especially bad. I couldn’t settle down. Even sitting in my chair, it felt like my blood was bubbling away, and I just couldn’t keep still.

lines.japanese: 早くも残務処理の四番目に「済」の字を打ちこみたかったけど、校則で携帯電話の使用は禁じられているから我慢した。
lines.english: I wanted to mark the fourth piece of unfinished business DONE right then, but school rules forbade the use of cell phones, so I restrained myself.

lines.japanese: 四列離れた斜め前の席。渡来さんは可動範囲の狭いポーズ人形みたいに、不自然なくらいまっすぐ背筋を伸ばして座っていた。
lines.english: Four rows away, in the seat diagonally ahead of mine, Watarai sat with her back unnaturally straight, like a stiff-jointed posing doll.

lines.japanese: その小さな頭が一度ちらりとこっちを向いた気がしたけど、僕はいつもの癖で慌てて目を逸らしてしまったので、実際にはただの思い上がりだったのかもしれない。
lines.english: I thought her small head turned briefly in my direction. But habit made me snatch my eyes away, so perhaps it had only been wishful thinking.

lines.japanese: 後ろの方から、誰かと誰かの声を殺した囁きが聞こえた。
lines.english: From somewhere behind me came the stifled whispers of two people.

lines.japanese: チャイムが鳴った瞬間（正確には回線を開いた際のノイズがスピーカーから漏れでた瞬間）、体の芯から熱が生じて全身へ広がった。全校集会で唐突に名前を呼ばれたときの感覚に似ていた。
lines.english: The instant the chime sounded—or, more precisely, the instant the speakers released the burst of static that came when the line opened—heat sprang from my core and spread through my body. It felt like hearing my name called without warning at a school assembly.

lines.japanese: 「委員長」
lines.english: “Class Rep.”

lines.japanese: 終わった。終わってしまった。
lines.english: It was over. It had ended.

lines.japanese: 始まる。始まってしまう。
lines.english: It was beginning. It was about to begin.

lines.japanese: 「委員長！　羽田君！」
lines.english: “Class Rep! Haneda!”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「終わりです。号令を」
lines.english: “Class is over. Lead the closing.”

lines.japanese: 「あ……すい、すいません」
lines.english: “Oh… s-sorry.”

lines.japanese: 舌打ちするような男子の声と、鼻で笑うような女子の声がした。僕は顔に血がのぼるのを実感しながら立ちあがった。
lines.english: A boy clicked his tongue; a girl gave a snort of laughter. Feeling the blood rise into my face, I stood.

lines.japanese: 起立、気をつけ、礼。
lines.english: Stand. Attention. Bow.

lines.japanese: いつもより通る声が出せたのは、羞恥心からか高揚感からか。
lines.english: My voice carried better than usual. Whether from humiliation or exhilaration, I could not tell.

lines.japanese: 恩田先生が教壇を降りると、教室はたちまち話し声と上履きの音と、勢いこんだ星野君が机の角にぶつかって張りあげた悲鳴とで賑わった。
lines.english: The moment Ms. Onda stepped down from the platform, the classroom filled with voices, the slap of indoor shoes, and Hoshino’s shriek as he charged into the corner of a desk.

lines.japanese: 僕は溜息じゃない一息を吐いて胸を撫でおろした。放課後が訪れたぐらいで歓声をあげるクラスメイトたちに、僕は今日初めて共感を覚えた。
lines.english: I released a breath that was not a sigh and felt the tension leave my chest. Today, for the first time, I understood the classmates who cheered merely because school was out.

lines.japanese: 立ったまま机の上に鞄を置いて、斜め前に目を走らせた。渡来さんもこっちを見ていた。染みついた習性でついまた思わず首を曲げてしまったけど、今日は目を合わせていいのだと気付いてすぐに向きなおった。
lines.english: Still standing, I placed my bag on the desk and glanced diagonally ahead. Watarai was looking at me too. Ingrained habit made me turn my head away again, but then I remembered: today I was allowed to meet her eyes. I faced her at once.

lines.japanese: 口元にかすかな笑みを湛えていた彼女は、人差し指を仰け反らせて、教室の前の扉を指した。ちょっと丸くなった目が「行こっか？」って言ってるみたいだった。
lines.english: A faint smile rested on her lips as she bent her index finger back and pointed to the door at the front of the classroom. Her eyes went a little round, like they were saying, ‘Wanna go?’

lines.japanese: 僕は平静を装って小さく頷く。だけど本当は子供みたいに大声で応えたかったんだ。
lines.english: I put on a calm face and gave a small nod. In truth, I wanted to shout my answer like a child.

lines.japanese: 「羽田ぁー」
lines.english: “Hanedaaa.”

lines.japanese: ところが三歩も進まないうちに、冷水みたいな女子の声に呼びとめられた。
lines.english: But before I had gone three steps, a girl’s voice like cold water stopped me.

lines.japanese: 「はぁ？　なんでよ、なに下校モード入ってんのあんた」
lines.english: “Huh? What’s with you? Who said you could switch into going-home mode?”
“…What?”

lines.japanese: 振りかえると副委員長が、眉をひそめて口の端を吊りあげていた。良くない予感がたれこめる。笑顔にもいろいろあると思った。
lines.english: I turned. The deputy class rep was frowning at me with one corner of her mouth drawn upward. A dark premonition gathered overhead. There were many kinds of smiles, I reflected.

lines.japanese: 「えじゃねーよ。卒文制作の準備！　今日から始めよ言ったの誰だよ」
lines.english: “Don’t ‘what’ me. We have to start getting the graduation anthology ready! Who said we’d begin today?”

lines.japanese: 「え……ああ、でも、高内さんやる気ないみたいだったし」
lines.english: “Oh… right. But you didn’t seem very interested, Takauchi.”

lines.japanese: 「ねえよ。バリねえよ。でも、やんなきゃなんねンだろ」
lines.english: “I’m not. I’m seriously not. But we gotta do it, don’t we?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それとも？　私やんなくていい？　マジで！　あんたひとりでやってくれんの？　あー、そうじゃん、よくね？　逆にソレよくね？」
lines.english: “Wait, or do we? Can I just skip it? Seriously? You’ll do the whole thing yourself? Oh, yeah, why not? That’s perfect. Actually, that’s way better, isn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 「いや……それは……困るけど……」
lines.english: “No… that would… be a problem…”

lines.japanese: 「……使えねー」
lines.english: “…You’re useless.”

lines.japanese: 舌打ちの音が聞こえて、僕は白い空を仰いだ。やっぱりこの部屋は今日も息苦しい。
lines.english: I heard her click her tongue and looked up at the white sky. This room was as suffocating as ever today.

lines.japanese: 「じゃーやるしかないじゃん。えっとー、昼メシ食ってー……ま、１時ぐらい？　そんぐらいに集ー合ー」
lines.english: “Then we’ve just gotta do it. Let’s see, I’ll eat lunch… so, one o’clock? We’ll meet up around then.”

lines.japanese: 高内さんは教室の時計を見上げながら一方的に告げた。困る。僕には僕の予定があるんだ。
lines.english: Takauchi said it like that was settled, looking up at the classroom clock. This was a problem. I had plans of my own.

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと待って。あの、それじゃさ、今からサッと始めない？　きょうは初日だし、簡単に概要だけ話しあって、軽く十分ぐらいで解散、でいいと思うんだ」
lines.english: “Wait. Why don’t we start right now and make it quick? It’s only the first day, so we can just go over the general plan and call it after ten minutes or so.”

lines.japanese: 「いやムリだから。私いまチョー腹減ってるし。も、がっつり入れねーと動けないもん」
lines.english: “No way. I’m starving right now. If I don’t get a real meal in me, I’m not moving.”

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ、明日からにしてもらえないかな。おれ、ちょっと今日は用事があって」
lines.english: “Then could we start tomorrow instead? I’ve got something I need to do today.”

lines.japanese: 「はァ！？　用事あるじゃねーだろナンダソレ自分だけェ！　ふざけ、おま、ほんっっっとジコチューだな。ちょっとさァ！　ねェ！　マジ少しはこっちの都合も考えてくんない！」
lines.english: “The hell? You don’t get to have plans—what is this, just you? Are you kidding me? God, you are so unbelievably selfish. Hey! I’m talking to you! Could you maybe think about what works for me for once?”

lines.japanese: 「うん……ごめん、悪いと思うんだけど……」
lines.english: “Yes… Sorry. I know it’s unfair, but…”

lines.japanese: 「んー、どしたこらー」
lines.english: “Hmm? What’s all this, then?”

lines.japanese: 下を向いて言葉を探していたら、古文の金子先生の口真似をした、泣きたくなるぐらい可愛い声が近付いてきた。
lines.english: As I stared at the floor, searching for words, an unbearably lovely voice approached, imitating Kaneko, our classical Japanese teacher.

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、べつに……」
lines.english: “Oh, no. It's nothing...”

lines.japanese: 来てほしくなかった。こんなふうに俯いてるところを見られたくなかった。
lines.english: I had not wanted her to come. I had not wanted her to see me hanging my head this way.

lines.japanese: 高内さんは鬱陶しげな目で渡来さんを一瞥したけど、その質問には答えず、僕に権高な声を浴びせた。
lines.english: Takauchi gave Watarai an irritated glance. Ignoring her question, she turned an imperious voice upon me.

lines.japanese: 「羽田さあ、おまえ自分から言っといてドタキャンとか、マジどんだけよ。俄然ムカつくわ。ふざけんな？」
lines.english: “Haneda, you’re the one who suggested this, and now you’re bailing? Seriously, what the hell? Now I’m actually pissed. You gotta be kidding me.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……分かったよ、じゃあ今日でいいよ……」
lines.english: “All right… Fine. We’ll do it today…”

lines.japanese: 僕は自棄になって承諾した。高内さんの厳しい言葉より渡来さんの優しい視線が痛くて、もうとにかく、速やかにこの場を収めてしまいたかったんだ。
lines.english: I gave up and agreed. Watarai’s gentle gaze hurt more than Takauchi’s harsh words, and by then I just wanted to wrap this up as fast as possible.

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth.*

lines.japanese: 「じゃ１時だからな。おめ、ぜってー来いよ。ブッチしたら担任に報告すっかんな」
lines.english: “One o’clock, then. You’d better show. If you ditch me, I’m telling our teacher.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんに肩をぶつける勢いで、副委員長は去っていった。彼女を待っていたらしいふたりの女子が、席を立ち慌ててあとを追っていった。
lines.english: The deputy class rep swept away, nearly shouldering Watarai aside. Two girls who had apparently been waiting for her scrambled from their seats and hurried after her.

lines.japanese: 「ん、んんっ……」
lines.english: “Mm—kh…”

lines.japanese: 窓の閉ざされた空間に、冷たい風が渡ってゆく。僕は喉にいがらっぽさを感じて咳払いした。
lines.english: A cold wind crossed that room of sealed windows. A rasp caught in my throat, and I cleared it.

lines.japanese: 「渡来さん、あの──っかふ、こふこふ、こふっ」
lines.english: “Watarai, I—khff, koff, koff—”

lines.japanese: また喉がからむ。僕は口を覆って、いくつか咳をした。
lines.english: My throat caught again. I covered my mouth and coughed several times.

lines.japanese: 空気が汚い。空気が薄い。空気が冷たい。
lines.english: The air was filthy. The air was thin. The air was cold.

lines.japanese: 「分かった。学級委員のお仕事だ？」
lines.english: “I understand. Class-rep duties?”

lines.japanese: なかば身を折るように咳きこんでいた僕の顔を、渡来さんは横から覗くように首を傾げた。
lines.english: As I coughed, doubled halfway over, Watarai tipped her head and peered into my face from the side.
“Yes…”

lines.japanese: 僕は自分の首を左手でぎゅっと絞め、そこに滞った咳のもとを力ずくで抑えようとした。
lines.english: I clamped my left hand around my throat and tried to throttle the cough lodged there into submission.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん……そういうわけだから……悪いけど今日は……」
lines.english: “Sorry… That’s how it is, so… I hate to do this, but today…”
“No—”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「──ってわけにもいかないんでしょ。うん、いいよべつに」
lines.english: “—is what I can’t very well say, can I? Sure. It’s fine.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは冗談を言っても表情を緩めなかった。僕の落胆が滑稽に思えるほどあっさりしていた。どうやら放課後への期待値には、僕とのあいだに大きな差があったみたいだ。
lines.english: Watarai didn’t even crack a smile at her own joke. She took it so lightly that my disappointment felt ridiculous. Apparently she’d been looking forward to after school a whole lot less than I had.

lines.japanese: 当たり前だ。僕にとってはたったひとりの渡来さんでも、彼女にとってはそこらをうごめく有象無象の中の男子Ａだ。
lines.english: Of course there was. To me she was the one and only Watarai; to her I was Boy A, one of the nameless multitude crawling everywhere.

lines.japanese: 僕は好きな女の子とのデートに胸弾ませていたけど、渡来さんはガイドを連れて巷の流行にひとつ触れようとしていただけだ。
lines.english: I’d been thrilled about a date with the girl I liked. Watarai just wanted a guide while she tried one thing people were into.

lines.japanese: 僕が駄目なら、彼女はゲームに詳しい他の誰かを選べばいいだけなんだ。自分から誘うのは苦手でも、誘ってくる相手ならきっと他に大勢いる。そうだ、誰か男と歩いてたって噂も、いつか耳にしたじゃないか。
lines.english: If I couldn’t do it, all she had to do was pick someone else who knew games. Even if she wasn’t good at asking people herself, there had to be plenty of guys who’d ask her. Right—I’d even heard that rumor about her walking with some guy once.

lines.japanese: 「ほんと……残念だな……」
lines.english: “It really is… a shame…”

lines.japanese: どこからか吹く木枯らしが見えない砂埃を運んできた。僕は首を絞める。力を込めて絞める。
lines.english: A winter gale from nowhere swept invisible dust through the room. I strangled my throat. Squeezed it with all my strength.

lines.japanese: 汚い風。目に砂が入ってちりちりと痛い。
lines.english: A filthy wind. Sand stung and smoldered in my eyes.

lines.japanese: 「おかしいな……なんでこうなるんだろう……」
lines.english: “It’s strange… How did it come to this…?”

lines.japanese: ごうごうと風の音がうるさい。首筋から後頭部にかけて、ゆっくりと重い力がのしかかってくる。
lines.english: The roar of the wind was deafening. A slow, heavy pressure descended from the nape of my neck across the back of my skull.

lines.japanese: 一方で、腹の奥がねじれたように鈍く痛む。僕は首と同時に、胃のあたりも掴んだ。力を込めて掴んだ。
lines.english: At the same time, a dull pain twisted deep in my belly. One hand still on my throat, I seized my stomach with the other. Gripped it hard.

lines.japanese: 「こんなはずじゃ……なかったんだけどな……」
lines.english: “This wasn’t… how it was supposed to go…”

lines.japanese: 「ねえ、なんか今日……風が強いよね……」
lines.english: “Doesn’t the wind seem… awfully strong today?”

lines.japanese: 「そういう日もある。ん」
lines.english: “There are days like that. Mm.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは労わるようなアルカイックスマイルでうんうんと頷いた。
lines.english: Watarai nodded and nodded, her archaic smile full of tender concern.

lines.japanese: 僕は咳きこみながらも、なんとかむりやり笑顔を返した。
lines.english: Still coughing, I somehow forced a smile in return.

lines.japanese: 本当にひどい砂埃で、開かない窓を恨まずにはいられない。
lines.english: The dust was truly terrible. I could not help resenting the windows that refused to open.

lines.japanese: 密室に吹きすさぶ風は、白い空まで届いているのか。
lines.english: Did the wind raging through this sealed room reach all the way to the white sky?

lines.japanese: そんなとき僕のポケットにあったのはいつだってペロリチョコ。コイン一枚おいしさ二倍、あの日の夕陽がよみがえる懐かしの甘さ──
lines.english: At times like this, there was always Perori Chocolate in my pocket. One coin, twice the deliciousness—the nostalgic sweetness that brings back that sunset—

lines.japanese: ──と思ったけど、朝食べてしまったからすでにポケットは空だった。
lines.english: —or so I thought. I had eaten it that morning. My pocket was already empty.
